summary: The Anglican Church in North America's catechism teaches that the Church is the whole community of faithful Christians in heaven and on earth, gathering in local congregations to worship in Word and Sacrament under the leadership of those God appoints, and that it is one, holy, catholic and apostolic. It names three ordained ministries, bishops, priests and deacons, and says bishops lead in preaching, teaching and shepherding, guard the faith, unity and discipline of the Church, and bless, confirm and ordain, following the apostles. The text read does not say who may be ordained.

points.question: How is the church governed?
points.answer: By three ordained ministries, bishops, priests and deacons. Bishops are chief pastors who lead in teaching, guard the faith and discipline of the Church, and ordain.

points.question: Where is the true church?
points.answer: The Church is the whole community of faithful Christians in heaven and on earth, which gathers locally to worship in Word and Sacrament, and is one, holy, catholic and apostolic.
